# Effectiveness of the Adjuvanted Recombinant Zoster Vaccine in Adults ≥50 Years in the United States _Open Access_
## Abstract
Background
Recombinant zoster vaccine (RZV) was approved for adults aged ≥50 years in the United States to prevent herpes zoster (HZ) and postherpetic neuralgia (PHN). This study evaluated real-world vaccine effectiveness (VE) of RZV in adults aged ≥50 years.
Methods
Among N = 102 766 (median age 68 years) who received 2 RZV doses (4 weeks–6 months apart), 48 028 (46.7%) had previously received zoster vaccine live; aVE was 73.9% (95% CI: 71.8%–75.8%) for HZ and 83.7% (95% CI: 75.1%–89.3%) for PHN. VE against HZ was comparable across individuals with concomitant vaccinations and different comorbidities.

...

Although pre-licensure randomized trials showed high RZV efficacy  [9 , 10 ], further effectiveness studies are needed  [11–13 ]. The reported 2-dose RZV effectiveness against HZ ranged between 70.1% (68.6%–71.5%) and 74% (73%–76%) in ≥65-year-olds and between 76% (75%–78%) and 85.5% (83.5%–87.3%) in ≥50-year-olds  [14–17 ].

...

The overall adjusted 2-dose RZV effectiveness in this study was 73.9% (71.8%–75.8%) over 4 years of follow-up (mean 2.5 years), whereas the previously reported values in adults aged ≥50 years were 83.5% (74.9%–89.2%) (median 2.0 years of follow-up)  [15 ], 85.5% (83.5%–87.3%) (median 7.0 months of follow-up)  [16 ], and 76% (75%–78%) (mean 3.2 years of follow-up in unvaccinated and 1.4 years in 2-dose vaccinated individuals)  [17 ].

excerpts:
# Efficacy and safety of the recombinant zoster vaccine: A systematic review and meta-analysis
## Abstract
Twenty three publications reporting on 14 studies were selected, including 2 pivotal RCTs in older immunocompetent adults (ZOE-50 and ZOE-70), 4 RCTs on immunocompromised patients (haematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT), haematological malignancies, solid tumour, and renal transplantation), and 8 observational studies.
Vaccine efficacy of RZV against herpes zoster (HZ) and postherpetic neuralgia (PHN) was very high in immunocompetent older adults (respectively 94% and 91.2% in adults ≥50 years and 91.3% and 88.8% in adults ≥70 years). However, the number needed to vaccinate (NNV) was relatively high (between 32 and 36 for HZ and between 261 and 335 for PHN).

# Effectiveness and safety of the recombinant zoster vaccine in adults aged ≥50 years with inflammatory bowel disease
## ABSTRACT
In the VE evaluation cohort (2-dose vaccinated: N = 872, unvaccinated: N = 2,550), overall adjusted VE in preventing HZ was 65.1% (95% CI, 24.8–83.8). In SCCS analysis, among 1,199 individuals who received ≥1 dose of RZV, there was no increased risk of IBD flare observed within 30 days after vaccination (RR: 0.80; 95% CI, 0.47–1.35). In adults aged ≥50 with IBD, 2 doses of RZV effectively prevented HZ without increasing flare risk.

...

## Introduction
Pre-licensure studies were not conducted specifically in populations with autoimmune disease. 17–20 However, a post-hoc analysis of 2 parallel randomized clinical trials of RZV showed a 90.5% vaccine efficacy against HZ in individuals with pre-existing potential immune-mediated diseases, but these trials excluded those who were considered immunocompromised or were receiving immunosuppressive treatments.

...

## Discussion
Our results on RZV effectiveness in individuals with IBD are comparable to findings from previous studies. A retrospective analysis using a US claims database between 2018 and 2021 reported an overall VE of 73.4% for 2-dose RZV against HZ among individuals aged ≥50 years with IBD (63.5% for UC and 85.7% for CD), ³⁸ while our study estimated VEs of 83.2% for UC and 43.6% for CD.

...

excerpts:
# Effectiveness of the Recombinant Zoster Vaccine in Adults Aged 50 and Older in the United States: A Claims-Based Cohort Study _Free_
## Abstract
Recombinant zoster vaccine effectiveness was 85.5% (95% CI, 83.5–87.3%) overall, with an effectiveness of 86.8% (95% CI, 84.6–88.7%) in individuals 50 to 79 years old compared with 80.3% (95% CI, 75.1–84.3%) in individuals aged 80 and older. In patients with a history of live zoster vaccine within 5 years of study inclusion, vaccine effectiveness was 84.8% (95% CI, 75.3–90.7%).

...

Recombinant zoster vaccine (RZV; Shingrix; GlaxoSmithKline) is a 2-dose subunit vaccine that was licensed by the Food and Drug Administration in 2017 for adults aged 50 or older  [16 ]. Approval for RZV was based on evidence from the Zoster Efficacy Study in Adults 50 Years of Age and Older (ZOE-50), which demonstrated a 97.2% reduction in HZ among adults aged 50 and older  [17 ].

...

## RESULTS
Overall adjusted vaccine effectiveness was 85.5% (95% CI, 83.5–87.3%), with an effectiveness of 86.8% (95% CI, 84.6–88.7%) in individuals aged 50 to 79 years old compared with 80.2% (95% CI, 75.1–84.3%) in individuals aged 80 and older. In the E-value analysis to assess the effect of unmeasured confounding on RZV effectiveness, the null E-value was 12.8. The estimates of vaccine effectiveness were similar by sex, race/ethnicity, and region subgroups.

...

## DISCUSSION
The RZV was approved for adults aged 50 and over following the results of the ZOE-50 study. In this trial, RZV had an overall efficacy between 96.6% and 97.9% among all age groups 50 and above  [17 ]. In a follow-up study in individuals aged 70 and above (ZOE-70), RZV efficacy was 89.8%  [27 ]. Given that the median age of individuals in this study was 72 years old at the index date, the observed effectiveness of RZV was still high, at 85.5%.
